title: Creamy White Chicken Enchiladas
imagePrompt: Ten flour tortilla rolls packed tightly seam-down in a 9×13 baking dish, smothered in an ivory sour cream sauce flecked with pale green chiles. The Monterey Jack on top has melted into a glossy sheet, freckled golden-brown and blistered in spots from a quick broil, with sauce bubbling up thick and creamy around the edges. One enchilada is pulled out, showing a cross-section of tender shredded chicken bound in creamy, cheesy filling. Scattered chopped cilantro and thin green onion rings add bright green against the white.
subtitle: Shredded chicken, cream cheese, and green chiles rolled in flour tortillas under a silky sour cream sauce.

ingredients.heading: Ingredients
ingredients.note: Based on The Country Cook's version, with a few upgrades from other popular recipes: cream cheese in the filling, milk in the sauce, chiles split between filling and sauce, and a little sauce under the rolls.
items: Filling
3 cups shredded cooked chicken (rotisserie is easiest)
4 oz cream cheese, softened
1 cup shredded Monterey Jack
Half of a 7 oz can diced green chiles (do not drain)
½ tsp ground cumin
½ tsp garlic powder
½ tsp salt + black pepper
Sauce
3 tbsp butter
½ small onion, finely diced
3 tbsp all-purpose flour
1½ cups chicken broth
½ cup whole milk
½ tsp ground cumin
½ tsp salt
Pinch cayenne (optional)
1 cup sour cream, at room temperature
Other half of the green chiles
Assembly
10 taco-size flour tortillas (about 8-inch)
1½ cups shredded Monterey Jack (for the top)
Fresh cilantro + sliced green onion (for serving)
ingredients.callout: Key rule: Sour cream goes in off the heat. If it boils, the sauce turns grainy.

substitutes: Boneless chicken breasts or thighs, poached and shredded

shoppingList.item: Cream cheese (4 oz, half a block)
Monterey Jack (10 oz, about 2½ cups shredded)
Diced green chiles (one 7 oz can or two 4 oz cans)

body.html: Mild, creamy, crowd-pleasing enchiladas. Chicken and cheese bound with cream cheese, rolled up, and baked under a roux-thickened sour cream and green chile sauce until bubbly and browned.

items: Mise en place — shred chicken, soften cream cheese, dice onion, shred cheese, split the chiles, measure sauce ingredients
Mix the filling — chicken, cream cheese, Jack, half the chiles, spices
Make the sauce — onion in butter, roux, broth + milk, then sour cream off the heat
Roll + sauce — thin layer of sauce under, rolls seam-down, rest of sauce over
Bake + broil at 350°F, then a quick broil for browned cheese

body.html: Why it works: The roux gives the sauce enough body to hold together in the oven, and milk makes it silkier than broth alone. Cream cheese keeps the filling moist.

items: Preheat the oven to 350°F; grease a 9×13 baking dish.
Set out the 4 oz cream cheese and 1 cup sour cream to come to room temperature.
Shred the chicken to make 3 cups. Shred 2½ cups Monterey Jack: 1 cup for the filling, 1½ cups for the top.
Open the green chiles and split them roughly in half: one half for the filling, one for the sauce.
Finely dice ½ small onion.
Measure the filling spices: ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp garlic powder, ½ tsp salt, pepper.
Measure the sauce: 3 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp flour, 1½ cups broth, ½ cup milk, ½ tsp cumin, ½ tsp salt, optional cayenne.
Gather a medium bowl, a medium saucepan, a whisk, and the 10 tortillas.

body.html: Room-temp sour cream: Cold sour cream hitting a hot sauce is the most common cause of curdling. Pull it out first.

items: In a medium bowl, mash the cream cheese with a fork until smooth.
Add the chicken, 1 cup Jack, half the chiles, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and a few grinds of pepper.
Stir until the chicken is evenly coated. Taste and adjust salt.

body.html: Cream cheese stiff? Microwave it 10–15 seconds so it blends instead of leaving lumps.

slides.title: Make the Sauce
slides.checkboxLabel: Sauce thickened, sour cream stirred in off heat

items: Melt 3 tbsp butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion; cook 3–4 min until soft, not browned.
Whisk in 3 tbsp flour; cook 1 min, whisking (don't let it brown).
Slowly whisk in broth, then milk, until smooth.
Simmer 2–3 min, whisking, until it coats a spoon. Stir in cumin, salt, and cayenne.
Take the pan off the heat. Whisk in the sour cream and the other half of the chiles.

body.html: Don't boil after the sour cream goes in. It should look like a pourable gravy. Too thick? Splash in more broth.

items: Spread about ½ cup sauce over the bottom of the baking dish.
Warm the tortillas: wrap in a damp paper towel, microwave 20–30 sec so they roll without cracking.
Spoon a heaping ⅓ cup filling down the center of each tortilla, roll it tight, and set it seam-side down. Pack them in snugly.
Pour the rest of the sauce over everything, covering the tortilla edges.
Sprinkle the remaining 1½ cups Jack over the top.

body.html: Cover the edges: Any exposed tortilla dries out and goes crunchy. Push sauce into the gaps.

items: Bake uncovered at 350°F for 20–25 min, until the sauce bubbles at the edges.
Optional: switch to broil (high) for 1–2 min until the cheese has golden spots. Watch it the whole time.
Rest 5 min so the sauce settles before serving.
Top with cilantro and green onion. Good with Mexican rice, refried beans, or a green salad.

body.html: Make-ahead: Assemble, cool the sauce completely, cover, and refrigerate up to 1 day or freeze up to 3 months. Let it come to room temp (or add 10–15 min) before baking.
